variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: An agentic AI system is software in which a model can choose the next step in a multi-step task, use tools, inspect results, and continue until a runtime stop condition is reached. The model may help decompose a goal and propose actions, but ordinary software still owns credentials, authorization, durable state, budgets, and execution.
variants.prompt: Match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Deterministic workflow
pairs.detail: Code owns the sequence and branches.
pairs.explanation: Code owns the sequence and branches. A model may classify or draft inside a step, but it does not decide the next operation. Prefer this when rules and transitions are known.

pairs.label: Bounded agent loop
pairs.detail: The model proposes the next step inside fixed tool, state, budget, and approval boundaries.
pairs.explanation: The model proposes the next step inside fixed tool, state, budget, and approval boundaries. Use it when run-time evidence changes which action is needed.

pairs.label: Multi-agent system
pairs.detail: Several model-driven workers coordinate through a manager, handoffs, or shared tasks.
pairs.explanation: Several model-driven workers coordinate through a manager, handoffs, or shared tasks. Add this only when specialization or parallel work improves measured outcomes enough to justify more failure paths.

variants.hint:
Deterministic workflow: Code owns the sequence and branches.

Bounded agent loop: The model proposes the next step inside fixed tool, state, budget, and approval boundaries.

Multi-agent system: Several model-driven workers coordinate through a manager, handoffs, or shared tasks.
variants.explanation: Each part has a distinct responsibility. Keeping these boundaries clear helps you find the place to change when the system behaves unexpectedly.

pairs.label: Outcome
pairs.detail: Grade authoritative environment state against task-specific success criteria.
pairs.explanation: Grade authoritative environment state against task-specific success criteria. Detect false-success claims where the response and external state disagree.

pairs.label: Trajectory
pairs.detail: Inspect tool selection, arguments, step count, retries, handoffs, and unnecessary actions.
pairs.explanation: Inspect tool selection, arguments, step count, retries, handoffs, and unnecessary actions. A correct result can still reveal an unsafe path.

pairs.label: Boundary
pairs.detail: Inject disallowed tools, oversized arguments, prompt injection, approval bypass, scope escalation, and budget pressure.
pairs.explanation: Inject disallowed tools, oversized arguments, prompt injection, approval bypass, scope escalation, and budget pressure.

pairs.label: Recovery
pairs.detail: Kill workers, duplicate deliveries, lose acknowledgements, expire approvals, and verify checkpoint, reconciliation, cancellation, and compensation behavior.

variants.prompt: What is the core invariant of a production agentic AI system?
options: The model may propose steps, but deterministic runtime controls decide what can execute, persist, retry, and stop.
Every task must be delegated to more than one model.
A tool call is trustworthy when the model explains why it selected the tool.
The run is complete whenever the model says it succeeded.

variants.prompt: Which approval design best protects a high-impact mutation?
options: Ask the model to approve its own proposal.
Show a generic confirmation generated from raw tool text.
Pause durable state and show canonical tool name, arguments, scope, and consequence to an authorized reviewer.
Approve every future call to the tool after one successful run.
variants.explanation: The reviewer needs exact, trusted details for the pending effect. Approval must bind to that call and survive pause and resume safely.
